answer: Under a one-identity-per-device enrollment policy, each PoA identity is bound to a key provisioned in an attested enclave; its MRENCLAVE identifies the measured code, while the remote-attestation quote lets verifiers check that measurement. A copied VM cannot reproduce the hardware-rooted proof, so an additional accepted identity requires another provisioned physical processor, not software duplication. crystal, yarrow, and vertex are payload labels, not trust anchors.
